intro: Improving searchability of docs is a critical task for technical writers who want their content to actually reach users. High-quality documentation often remains hidden from search engines, leading to a discoverability crisis where valuable information sits unread in a digital library with no entrance.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of low discoverability

When your documentation is not searchable, you pay a steep price in both time and team morale. You spend hours writing clear, accurate guides that no one finds. This forces your support team to answer the same questions repeatedly. The cost is not just your time, but the wasted effort of the entire organization.

Most technical writers work in silos. They focus on accuracy while marketing teams focus on brand visibility. These goals often clash. Marketing wants high-level keywords, but users want specific answers to technical problems. If your page titles are just internal identifiers like 'Section 4.2', search engines will never rank them for what users actually type.

items: Siloed teams prevent knowledge sharing between SEO and technical writers.
Internal naming conventions confuse search algorithms.
Rapid product cycles leave no time for keyword research or maintenance.
AI-driven search engines require structured data that many wikis lack.

blocks.text: You do not need a massive budget to fix these issues. Start by changing your titles to be task-based. Instead of 'Module 10', use 'How to configure your API key'. Place the answer at the very top of the page. Search engines love direct answers because they satisfy user intent immediately.
Use your support tickets as a keyword research tool. If five users ask how to reset a password in one week, that is your next article title.
blocks.title: Use your data

blocks.text: Managing your SEO on a Mac

Managing SEO on macOS requires a steady workflow. You can use tools like Screaming Frog for deep audits or Ahrefs for tracking keywords. If you use Windows-native tools like MadCap Flare, remember to use virtualization software like Parallels Desktop to keep your Mac workflow consistent.
How Lazur helps you write better docs

faq.question: Does SEO optimization require a marketing degree?
faq.answer: No. You only need to understand the intent behind user searches. Focus on answering their specific questions clearly.

faq.question: How often should I update documentation for SEO?
faq.answer: Review your top-performing support tickets monthly. Update your documentation whenever you see a recurring pattern in user questions.
